barossa-valley-1.name: Penfolds Barossa Valley
barossa-valley-1.bio: Penfolds' Nuriootpa cellar door runs tastings and a make-your-own-blend session at the winery behind Grange.
barossa-valley-1.coordinates_source: resolve-pin MEDIUM: OSM node 2800392101 craft=winery 'Penfolds Barossa Valley Cellar Door', Nuriootpa  ""
barossa-valley-1.notes: Prices are Time Out's listings (Make Your Own Blend $95, Barossa Ultimate Tasting $100), not the official page; bookings needed for guided experiences, guests 18+. Entering the cellar door is not itself ticketed. Penfolds URL is the homepage (deep links return 410); title 'Sites-PenfoldsAU-Site' does not name the place, so check in browser.

barossa-valley-2.name: Seppeltsfield Winery
barossa-valley-2.bio: Historic Seppeltsfield estate, reached along a palm-lined avenue, offers cellar tours and tastings including 100-year-old tawny.
barossa-valley-2.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 7129624923 "Seppeltsfield Cellar Door" (craft=winery, tourism=attraction), 100 m from the Wikipedia point
barossa-valley-2.notes: Official site loaded (title 'Seppeltsfield Barossa'). Cheapest listed guided experience: Milestone Wine Tour and Tasting from A$180 (experienceoz listing, 2025); official pages state only 'tasting fees apply'. Walking the estate is free via the Self-Guided History Experience podcast stops (price not shown; unverified). Estate open 10am daily, closed Good Friday and Christmas/Boxing/New Year's Day.

barossa-valley-3.name: Whispering Wall
barossa-valley-3.bio: The curved 1903 Barossa Reservoir dam wall carries a whisper along its 144 m length to the far end.
barossa-valley-3.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: Wikipedia "Barossa Dam" coordinates (6 dp); OSM node 937530476 "Whispering Wall" (tourism=attraction) is 110 m away on the same wall
barossa-valley-3.ticket_note: SA Water reserve; no operator site found
barossa-valley-3.notes: Free admission and parking per tourism listings; closes on Total Fire Ban days (not in bio).

barossa-valley-4.name: Menglers Hill Lookout
barossa-valley-4.bio: Hilltop lookout above the Barossa Valley, with a sculpture park beside the car park.
barossa-valley-4.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 952758657 "Menglers Hill Lookout" (tourism=viewpoint); the Sculpture Park is OSM artwork 70 m away
barossa-valley-4.ticket_note: Council-run roadside lookout; no official page checked

barossa-valley-5.name: Barossa Museum
barossa-valley-5.bio: Local-history museum in Tanunda's Old Telegraph Station, with displays on the Barossa's settlers and heritage.
barossa-valley-5.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 9802952015 "Barossa Museum" (tourism=museum, Mill Street)
barossa-valley-5.ticket_note: Official site not reachable (barossamuseum.org.au failed to load; barossa.com listing 403)
barossa-valley-5.notes: Adult $5, child $2 per the Barossa Visitor Centre heritage factsheet (Dec 2024). Opening days differ by source (Mon/Thu/Fri/Sat 10-3 vs Fri/Mon 12-4), check before relying.

barossa-valley-6.name: Springton
barossa-valley-6.bio: Village best known for the Herbig Family Tree, a hollow red gum up to 500 years old where a settler family once lived.
barossa-valley-6.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 1953967515 "Springton" (place=town); Herbig Family Tree is OSM node 3924796969 at -34.7100031,139.0885377, 340 m away
barossa-valley-6.ticket_note: Town with no single steward; the Herbig tree is run by the J. F. Herbig Memorial Family Association (site not verified)
barossa-valley-6.notes: Herbig Family Tree: free entry, donations welcomed, site always open; about 7 m across and 24 m tall; tree age quoted 300-500 years.

barossa-valley-7.name: Angaston
barossa-valley-7.bio: Eastern Barossa town with a heritage main street, galleries and food producers.
barossa-valley-7.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 180957512 "Angaston" (place=village); the Wikipedia point (-34.5, 139.05) is a rounded memory-style pin and was not used

barossa-valley-8.name: Eden Valley
barossa-valley-8.bio: High-country wine village with a scenic lookout on Burkes Hill and a historic main street.
barossa-valley-8.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 3924785645 "Eden Valley Lookout" (tourism=viewpoint, on Burkes Hill Road); the village itself is about 1.3 km south (CFS at -34.6424,139.0979); the OSM place=locality 'Eden Valley' node is 4 km east and a locality centroid, not used
barossa-valley-8.notes: Pinned on the lookout since the spot is categorised viewpoint and the bio leads with it.

barossa-valley-9.name: Lyndoch
barossa-valley-9.bio: Southern gateway village of the Barossa, with wineries and a bakery-lined main street.
barossa-valley-9.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 193757707 "Lyndoch" (place=village)

barossa-valley-10.name: Greenock
barossa-valley-10.bio: Heritage village with a 27-site Historical Walk and an aviation museum nearby.
barossa-valley-10.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 180957524 "Greenock" (place=village)
barossa-valley-10.notes: Walk site count and aviation museum are from Atlas's draft, from tourism sources; not re-verified here.

barossa-valley-11.name: Nuriootpa
barossa-valley-11.bio: The Barossa's commercial centre and a base for the valley's wineries, with shops and services.
barossa-valley-11.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 180957503 "Nuriootpa" (place=town)
barossa-valley-11.notes: Bio kept generic; Wikivoyage/SA Tourism list it as a base for the valley.

barossa-valley-12.name: Kapunda
barossa-valley-12.bio: Copper-mining town on the Barossa's western edge, with Cornish mining heritage, a local museum and Gundry's Hill Lookout.
barossa-valley-12.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM via overpass.openstreetmap.fr (Overpass main instances down; Nominatim/Photon rate-limited): node 180957537 "Kapunda" (place=town)
barossa-valley-12.notes: Copper mined 1844-1879 (Wikipedia). Map the Miner statue is a separate spot (barossa-valley-13).

barossa-valley-13.name: Map the Miner
barossa-valley-13.bio: A 7 m bronze statue of a Cornish miner at Kapunda's southern entrance, honouring the town's copper-mining history.
barossa-valley-13.ticket_note: Roadside statue with no single operator or official page.
barossa-valley-13.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=artwork 'Map the Miner' (Nominatim), 14 m from the Wikipedia point: HIGH

barossa-valley-14.name: Gawler
barossa-valley-14.bio: Town 40 km north of Adelaide, once a resting stop on the road to the Kapunda and Burra copper mines.
barossa-valley-14.ticket_note: A town with no single steward.
barossa-valley-14.coordinates_source: Nominatim place centre for Gawler (admin boundary linked to the town node), 70 m from the Wikipedia point; HIGH
notes: Marginal as a visitor stop: Wikivoyage's Gawler page lists only the National Trust Museum (dead link) and a jockey club under Do, and no See entries; kept because the coverage judge kept it. Owner may want to review it (low visit value, a gateway town).

barossa-valley-15.name: Warren Conservation Park
barossa-valley-15.bio: Conservation park of stringybark and box woodland with three steep walking trails, one a section of the Heysen Trail.
barossa-valley-15.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: osm leisure=nature_reserve (nominatim) "Warren Conservation Park"
notes: pin: LOW (provisional point on the mapped Warren Tower Hike inside the park; the entrance car park should be taken from the NPWS park map)
NPWS page: free entry, open daily, closed on Catastrophic Fire Danger days; tracks steep, for experienced walkers.

clare-valley-1.name: Sevenhill Cellars
clare-valley-1.bio: The Clare Valley's first winery, built by Jesuits in 1851, with a cellar door and the landmark St Aloysius Church.
clare-valley-1.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=winery node 'Sevenhill Winery' (Overpass); the Commons photo median is 1.1 km away at the village green: MEDIUM
notes: No Wikipedia article for Sevenhill Cellars (the draft's wiki title is a red link), so no wiki field.
Cellar door open daily 10am-5pm; entry is free, tasting fees ($10 Inigo range, $30 premium range) are waived on a wine purchase and are an optional extra, so not recorded as the cost.
Church interior access not separately confirmed on the cellar door page; the church is the landmark on the village green.

clare-valley-2.name: Riesling Trail
clare-valley-2.bio: A 35 km walking and cycling trail along a former railway line from Auburn to Barinia, passing cellar doors.
clare-valley-2.coordinates_source: OSM trail midpoint (4.9 km, 'Mawson Trail Network: Riesling Trail' segment, Nominatim) about 2 km from the middle of the 35 km route; the whole route was not retrievable (Overpass overloaded): MEDIUM
notes: Length and Auburn-Barinia extent from the Clare Valley Tourism directory; trail site title confirmed: 'Walk, run or ride the Riesling Trail from Auburn to Barinia'.

clare-valley-3.name: Martindale Hall
clare-valley-3.bio: Georgian-style mansion of 32 rooms built in 1879 near Mintaro, open for self-guided tours and seen in Picnic at Hanging Rock.
clare-valley-3.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: OSM way 220684351 Martindale Hall (historic building); Wikipedia -33.9378,138.7294  ""
notes: Adult admission $20 (children $10) from the hall's own site; the surrounding conservation park is free entry (NPWS). Open 10am-4pm Wednesday to Monday, closed Tuesdays, daily in school holidays (NPWS) - covered in the Clare Valley tips.
resolve-pin.py itself returned LOW (Nominatim rate-limited, Overpass down); point taken from Overpass mirror plus Wikipedia.

clare-valley-4.name: Mintaro
clare-valley-4.bio: Heritage village of slate and stone buildings, founded in 1849 as a rest stop for bullock teams hauling copper from Burra.
clare-valley-4.ticket_note: A village with no single steward.
clare-valley-4.coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py MEDIUM: Nominatim place centre for Mintaro (admin boundary), 250 m from the Commons photo median and 380 m from the Wikipedia point

clare-valley-5.name: Spring Gully Conservation Park
clare-valley-5.bio: Conservation park near Clare where a walk from Blue Gum Lookout leads to an 18 m waterfall that runs after rain.
clare-valley-5.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=viewpoint node 'Blue Gum Lookout' (Overpass), the park's main lookout, 1 km from the park centroid: MEDIUM
notes: NPWS: free entry, open daily, closed on Catastrophic Fire Danger days; waterfall is seasonal.

clare-valley-6.name: Neagles Rock Short Walk
clare-valley-6.bio: A 1 km loop of about 45 minutes through grassy hillsides and red rock outcrops to a lookout over the Clare Valley.
clare-valley-6.ticket_note: Council walking trail; Clare Valley Tourism's directory page is a regional listing, not the steward, so no ticketUrl.
clare-valley-6.coordinates_source: OSM highway=path 'Neagles Rock Short Walk' (way centre, Overpass); the lookout node is 70 m away at -33.849094,138.607756: MEDIUM
notes: The walk is a 1 km loop, so the pin is the centre of one of its two mapped path segments, which lies on the path.

clare-valley-7.name: Auburn
clare-valley-7.bio: Small heritage town on the Wakefield River at the southern end of the Clare Valley, where the Riesling and Rattler Trails meet.
clare-valley-7.ticket_note: A town with no single steward.
clare-valley-7.coordinates_source: Nominatim place centre for Auburn, 48 m from the Wikipedia point: HIGH

clare-valley-8.name: Bungaree Station
clare-valley-8.bio: Sheep station founded in 1841 near Clare, with a self-guided tour of the village-like historic complex and its woolshed.
clare-valley-8.coordinates_source: OSM node 'Bungaree Station' (Overpass), same point as resolve-pin.py MEDIUM
notes: Self-guided tour $17.50 per adult for day visitors (under 12 free with an adult), daily 10am-4pm except private functions; guided tours need 20+ people.
The OSM node is a named locality node for the station, not the homestead; within a few hundred metres of the tour buildings (Bungaree Road, Clare).

clare-valley-9.name: Rattler Trail
clare-valley-9.bio: A 19 km walking and cycling trail from Riverton to Auburn, passing vineyards and farms, that joins the Riesling Trail.
clare-valley-9.ticket_note: Council-managed trail; no single official page found, and Clare Valley Tourism's directory page is a regional listing.
clare-valley-9.coordinates_source: OSM trail midpoint (6.9 km 'Rattler Trail' segment, Nominatim), the longest segment and near the middle of the 19 km route: MEDIUM

clare-valley-10.name: Blyth
clare-valley-10.bio: Mid North town with a community mosaic on a cafe wall and the 4.4 km Dean Nicolle Eucalypt Walk on the old rail corridor.
clare-valley-10.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM node 2128342271 place=village "Blyth" (wikipedia en:Blyth, South Australia); Wikipedia's own point is a rounded 8-dp town point 1.5 km away. Mosaic is on Blyth Cafe's north wall (~200 m south), not pinned.
clare-valley-10.notes: Draft bio named Brooks Lookout; no source found for it, so it is left out. Mosaic (8 Harley Street, Mike Tye design, 30+ volunteers) from clarevalley.com.au/directory/the-blyth-mosaic; walk from Wikipedia and clarevalley listing, opened Aug 2025, starts at the northern edge beside Rail Corridor Road. Town is judged a stop on the mosaic and the walk.

clare-valley-11.name: Farrell Flat Silo Art
clare-valley-11.bio: Silo mural of the last train through town, painted in 2020 by Jarrod Soden and Matthew Knights, on Patterson Terrace.
clare-valley-11.coordinates_source: HIGH: OSM way 603212964 man_made=silo (middle of three silos) and Commons photo 'Painted Silos viewed from the Pub at Farrell Flat' 80 m away
clare-valley-11.notes: Source: clarevalley.com.au/directory/farrell-flat-silo-art (completed Nov 2020, 30 m tall). Draft's 'first of the Clare Valley Silo Art Trail' dropped: source says first painted in the region. No Wikipedia article (wiki omitted).

burra-1.name: Burra Mine Site
burra-1.bio: Open-air Monster Mine copper-mining site with Morphett's Engine House, a powder magazine, lookouts and Peacock's Chimney.
burra-1.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM node 2130285523 'Burra Mine Site - National Trust' (tourism=museum); Morphett's Engine House node is 130 m away
burra-1.notes: Entered with the Burra Heritage Passport key (adult $35, $50 refundable key deposit, valid two days; visitburra.com.au/?p=1481 -> visitburra.com.au/burra-heritage-pass/). The passport's price is shown on each of its sites; National Trust page says admission is as part of the passport.

burra-2.name: Redruth Gaol
burra-2.bio: National Trust gaol on Tregony Street with cells and exercise yards, entered with the Burra Heritage Passport key.
burra-2.coordinates_source: HIGH: OSM way 223968806 'Redruth Gaol' and Wikipedia -33.6645,138.933
burra-2.notes: Entered with the Burra Heritage Passport key (adult $35, $50 refundable key deposit, valid two days; visitburra.com.au/?p=1481 -> visitburra.com.au/burra-heritage-pass/). The passport's price is shown on each of its sites; National Trust page says admission is as part of the passport.

burra-3.name: Miners Dugouts
burra-3.bio: Creek-bank dugouts on Burra Creek where early miners lived, dug in the 1840s and opened with the passport key.
burra-3.notes: Entered with the Burra Heritage Passport key (adult $35, $50 refundable key deposit, valid two days; visitburra.com.au/?p=1481 -> visitburra.com.au/burra-heritage-pass/). The passport's price is shown on each of its sites; National Trust page says admission is as part of the passport. National Trust: around 600 dugouts were excavated along Burra Creek between 1846 and 1851. No Wikipedia article (wiki omitted).

burra-4.name: Burra Railway Station
burra-4.bio: Restored 1870 station run by volunteers, with railway displays, the 1917 dining carriage Edie and guided tours.
burra-4.coordinates_source: HIGH: OSM node 4923247862 'Burra Railway Station' and Wikipedia -33.6742,138.9196
burra-4.notes: Draft said free via the Burra Passport; the visitburra.com.au/burra-railway-station/ page says it is volunteer-run, entry by donation, open daily 11:00-13:00 and closed at 35 C or above, so it is not part of the passport price. ticketUrl title 'Home | Burrarailwaystation' (Friends of the Burra Railway Station).

burra-5.name: Bon Accord Mine Complex
burra-5.bio: National Trust museum on the Bon Accord mine site, with mining relics, a Monster Mine model and a working blacksmith shop.
burra-5.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM node 2130283553 'Bon Accord Cottage - National Trust' (tourism=museum), the Bon Accord Mining Museum site
burra-5.notes: Adult $5, concession $4, under 16 and NTSA members free, passport key holders $2 (National Trust page, title 'Bon Accord Mine Museum - National Trust'). Closes above 38 C or on severe fire-danger days. No Wikipedia article (wiki omitted).

lake-bumbunga.name: Lake Bumbunga
lake-bumbunga.bio: Salt lake beside Highway 1 at Lochiel whose colour shifts from pink to white, with a lookout and the Loch-Eel sculpture.
lake-bumbunga.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM node 9753934217 tourism=viewpoint on the Lochiel shore; Loch-Eel sculpture node is 230 m east. Wikipedia's point is the lake centroid, 3 km away
lake-bumbunga.notes: Colour varies with salinity and season (clarevalley.com.au/directory/lake-bumbunga; Wikipedia: pinker in spring than winter). Salt is mined there, so not all of it is open access.

eudunda-silo-art.name: Eudunda Silo Art
eudunda-silo-art.bio: 30 m silo mural from 2021 by Sam Brooks, drawn from Colin Thiele's novel The Sun on the Stubble and a Ngadjuri storybook.
eudunda-silo-art.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM way 535062782 man_made=silo in the Eudunda silo group (railway side), consistent with Commons photo 70 m away
eudunda-silo-art.notes: Source: clarevalley.com.au/directory/eudunda-silo-art (parking on Railway Parade). Which silo carries the mural is not given; pin is the middle of the group. No Wikipedia article (wiki omitted).

terowie.name: Terowie
terowie.bio: Historic railway town on the Barrier Highway where General MacArthur stopped in 1942, with a Historic Walk of 35 buildings.
terowie.coordinates_source: MEDIUM: OSM node 2316964266 place=village 'Terowie' (wikipedia en:Terowie, South Australia); Wikipedia's own point is 500 m south
terowie.ticket_note: No single steward: an open town; the volunteer visitor centre opens the museum buildings on request.
terowie.notes: Building count 35 from several guides (one says 39); MacArthur layover 20 March 1942 per guides. Railway station node is 330 m east.

bundaleer-forest.name: Bundaleer Reservoir Reserve
bundaleer-forest.bio: SA Water reservoir reserve near Jamestown with loop trails, kayaking, fishing (permit needed) and picnic areas.
bundaleer-forest.coordinates_source: resolve-pin MEDIUM: OSM node 2321806062 tourism=picnic_site 'Bundaleer Arboretum Picnic Area' in Bundaleer Forest Reserve (w351751149)  ""
bundaleer-forest.ticket_note: SA Water page blocks scripts (Cloudflare); URL taken from search results, title unchecked.
bundaleer-forest.notes: pin: LOW. Renamed from 'Bundaleer Forest' (id kept): the listing the draft cites is Bundaleer Reservoir Reserve. Open sunrise to sunset, free parking and toilets, closed on Total Fire Ban days; SA Water lists a 4.5 km Reservoir Loop, 7 km Boundary Loop and 6 km Woods Loop; fishing permit needed; no dogs; kayaks and canoes only. The Bundaleer Forest campground and picnic ground (-33.278,138.571) is a different part of the forest 1.5 km east.

diggers-walk-belalie-creek.name: Diggers Walk Belalie Creek
diggers-walk-belalie-creek.bio: Creek-side heritage trail in Jamestown built by returned WWI servicemen, with interpretive displays and picnic spots.
diggers-walk-belalie-creek.coordinates_source: LOW: the route is not in OSM or Wikipedia; point is the creek-side swing bridge/park in central Jamestown from a Commons geotagged photo, not the route midpoint
diggers-walk-belalie-creek.notes: pin: LOW. Owner or a local map should supply the walk's route/midpoint. Source: flindersandoutback.com.au listing (built by returned servicemen after WWI, restored with interpretive displays, Sir Hubert Wilkins story; picnic and barbecue).
diggers-walk-belalie-creek.ticket_note: Council-managed open trail with no single operator page found.

jamestown-mural-walk-and-outdoor-gallery.name: Jamestown Mural Walk and Outdoor Gallery
jamestown-mural-walk-and-outdoor-gallery.bio: Self-guided walk past heritage-building murals on Jamestown's main streets, ending at an outdoor gallery on Ayr Street.
jamestown-mural-walk-and-outdoor-gallery.coordinates_source: resolve-pin LOW: Middle of the east section of Ayr Street, Jamestown (OSM street geometry, ways 787528736/787531712), near Jamestown Magic Cave attraction node  (provisional)

notes.pin: Outdoor Gallery at the east end of Ayr Street, Jamestown; walk starts at the visitor outlet on Ayr Street. Pin the gallery or the middle of the Ayr Street murals.
notes.cost: Free, outdoor street walk (no price stated on the listing).

jamestown-mural-walk-and-outdoor-gallery.ticket_note: No single steward site verified; the listing is a tourism-board page, not an operator site.

bowman-park.name: Bowman Park
bowman-park.bio: Public park near Crystal Brook with river red gums, a spring-fed brook, a nature playground and a Heysen Trail section.
bowman-park.coordinates_source: resolve-pin MEDIUM: OSM node 1456514352 amenity=parking "Bowman's Park" off Bowman Park Road, Crystal Brook  ""

notes.pin: Draft point is Wikipedia's rounded article coordinate (park centroid); re-pin to the park's car park or day-use area about 5 km NE of Crystal Brook.
notes.cost: Public park open sunrise to sunset; Wikipedia states no fee; not on parks.sa.gov.au (404), so council-run; treated as free.
notes.region: Near Crystal Brook, about 60 km from Clare; Wikipedia places it in the Mid North; Flinders/Yorke region call is the owner's.
notes.dropped_from_bio: 1850s homestead ruins not confirmed in a fetched source, so left out.

bowman-park.ticket_note: Not an NPWS park (parks.sa.gov.au 404); council page pirie.sa.gov.au/bowman-park blocked by bot wall.

held.reason: Jamestown Railway Station Museum: no cost or official site found. Unblocks on a price or source.

entry.bio: Local-history museum in Jamestown's 1885 railway station, with an 1870s carriage and displays on R.M. Williams.

notes.cost: Entry fee and any official site not stated on the listing; unverified.
